title: Avoiding Biases due to Similarity Assumptions in Node Embeddings

problem.claim: Node embeddings must represent graph structure, but similarity assumptions about unlinked nodes can introduce systematic biases and create privacy and dynamic-graph difficulties.

gap.claim: Existing methods that rely on similarities between unlinked or far-off nodes may expose risks to fairness and privacy and may be difficult to apply in dynamic graphs.

contributions.claim: The authors propose NEWS, a node embedding method that makes no similarity assumptions.
NEWS is parameter-free, supports fast link prediction, and has linear complexity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Comparisons against several existing methods on 21 real-world networks reportedly show that avoiding similarity assumptions does not significantly affect accuracy.
Code is reported as available in the cited repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Node embeddings represent graph structure using vectors for nodes, with adjacency as the basic structure.
Recent methods assume similarity among unlinked nodes, which can create systematic group biases and practical difficulties under privacy constraints and in dynamic graphs.
NEWS has no parameters, supports rapid link prediction, and has linear complexity.
The authors report accuracy comparisons on 21 real-world networks and provide code.

source_observation.claim: Similarity assumptions about unlinked nodes can create systematic group biases and raise privacy-related difficulties.

interpretation.claim: Removing an assumption that is not required by the basic graph structure may reduce fairness and privacy risks.

application.claim: When designing graph representations for sensitive or changing networks, evaluate whether inferred similarities are necessary and whether they introduce group or privacy risks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that avoiding similarity assumptions preserves accuracy in all datasets or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the NEWS algorithm, training procedure, or embedding construction.
The abstract does not identify the 21 networks, evaluation metrics, comparison methods, or quantitative accuracy results.
The abstract does not provide evidence quantifying privacy or fairness improvements.
